For Moses, the high priest, God commanded him to send out the people, having measured the power of human nature and seeing the ministry of preaching as greater, said 'I am weak-voiced and slow-tongued'. Similarly, Jeremiah, sent to prophesy, cried out 'I do not know how to speak, for I am young'. For even the saints, speaking such things, appear to be examples of piety, but this manner of fear is not small or harmless to the weak. For God comforts us and encourages us to cast out fear, saying to Moses 'Who gave a mouth to man, and who made one mute and deaf, seeing and blind? Is it not I, the Lord God? Now go, and I will open your mouth'. And to Jeremiah, 'Do not say "I am young", for you will go to all whom I send you, and you will speak all that I command you'. Therefore, I, a humble caller to the schema of priesthood, fearing the written 'Speak and do not be silent', necessarily come to write these things. For God's judgment has well delivered our life, and towards the heavenly monasteries, the memory of our father Theophilus, who was bishop (according to the steward of all, I am ashamed to write), the succession of the episcopate has fallen to me, the least. Hearing Paul writing…

Woe is me if I do not preach, for I am compelled by fear and weakness to proclaim; our holy things shine forth, and we are cleansed and purified; it is necessary to say to those still in wickedness to cleanse their hands and purify their hearts; the prophet will preach to those who have escaped the shame of sin and follow a life of love, saying 'Arise, Jerusalem, for your light has come and the glory of the Lord has risen upon you'; for people have become diverse and multiform in wickedness, and are overcome by the darkness of ignorance, falling into deep sin; the Psalmist necessarily says to God, 'Heed us, guide us, appear before us, and save us'; when we are lying down and have fallen, and perceive Him coming to us in due time, we cry out 'Why have you withdrawn from us, Lord, and overlooked us in times of trouble?' for the Savior has not yet taken on our likeness, and is far from us according to the word of His incarnation; and there are many intervals between human nature and the Word of God

I am earth and ashes; the prophet Isaiah speaks about the existence of the Only-Begotten; what generation will describe it? The Savior, born of a woman, appeared to us, who were suffering much affliction, to save the human being born of a woman, and having freed us from the bonds of death, teaches us to say: Where is your victory, death? Where is your sting, Hades? For he not only gives us the gift of resurrection, but also destroys the sting of Hades, that is, sin; he says: Behold, I have given you authority to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing will harm you; this is one of the achievements of our Savior's presence; therefore, all dignity on earth is governed; the darkness of ignorance has been dispelled; the Psalmist, foreseeing this with the power of the divine Spirit, said: Justice and abundance of peace will arise in his days, until the moon is no more; if we, being enemies, are reconciled to God through the death of his Son, an abundance of peace will arise for us; when this happens, it is necessary for the moon to be abolished, that is, the ruler of night and darkness, called moon here in a figurative sense; therefore, such great and numerous lights shine for us, and the light of our divine festival shines, and again the bright festival draws us to itself

It is more evident that one should depart from the most shameful things, advising and saying: 'Wash and become clean, remove wickedness from your souls.' For if the Proverb writer is wise, saying: 'There is a time for everything,' and a season for every matter, how can we not reasonably agree that this time is an enemy of all wickedness? It calls only those things that also know how to honor the divine law, and to those who have used it, it gives the vote of confidence to be brave. Those who want to contend in the present life, buying the title at great financial loss, and sweating in the contest, honor the winner with other wealthy prizes, but the gratitude is small, and the enjoyment only goes as far as the things of this life. The judge of the contest of the righteous is God, who gives to the pious things that the eye has not seen, and the ear has not heard, and that have not entered the human heart. For those whose thought is beyond nature, it is found through their works, and the manner of their gift surpasses human understanding. Having shown a way of life foreign to the many and unknown due to difficulty, they will find honor equal to their deeds, and having experienced the immense philanthropy of the Master, they will delight in goods beyond nature. Let us then also call the lovers of piety to the annual contest of labors, and the prophet says…

Sound the trumpet in Zion, sanctify a fast, proclaim a solemn assembly, a great and piercing call, the sacred trumpet of the Church, a clear and most prominent proclamation of our holy feast, announcing its presence, God speaking to Moses, the high priest, to make two silver trumpets, to assemble and summon the congregation, the Church's word is twofold, one calling the ignorant to the correct understanding of divine doctrines, the other advising against the foolishness of works, the trumpets are to be made of silver, symbolizing the brilliance and purity of the word, guiding away from error and heresy, the word should flow from us like a stream, calling the distant to the lawgiver's will, sanctifying the fast, proclaiming the healing, as the prophet says, how can we become workers of such things, how can we fulfill the divine command, avoiding evil, shunning shameful things, and striving to do the things that sanctify those who fast

Let the disciple of Christ come among us, teach the manner of fasting, we will hear him speaking; this is a pure and undefiled fast before God and Father: to visit orphans and widows in their affliction; to keep oneself unspotted from the world; it is easy to find out how and in what manner we will fulfill the aforementioned; for I think it is sufficient for those who are well-minded and also the law of nature itself, teaching to hate what seems to be contrary to divine commands, and persuading to hold the will of the lawgiver in us
pass_b_english: The high priest Moses, when God commanded him to send out the people, measured the power of human nature and saw that the ministry of preaching was greater. He said, 'I am weak-voiced and slow-tongued.'
Similarly, the blessed Jeremiah, when sent to prophesy, cried out, 'I do not know how to speak, for I am young.'
Even the saints, who speak such things, appear to be examples of piety, but this manner of fear is not small or harmless to the weak.

For God comforts us and encourages us to cast out fear, saying to Moses, 'Who gave a mouth to man, and who made one mute and deaf, seeing and blind? Is it not I, the Lord God? Now go, and I will open your mouth.'
And to Jeremiah, 'Do not say "I am young", for you will go to all whom I send you, and you will speak all that I command you.'
Therefore, I, a humble caller to the schema of priesthood, fearing the written 'Speak and do not be silent', necessarily come to write these things.
For God's judgment has well delivered our life, and towards the heavenly monasteries, the memory of our father Theophilus, who was bishop, has fallen to me, the least.
Hearing Paul write, 'Woe is me if I do not preach the gospel,' I am compelled by fear and weakness to proclaim.
Our holy things shine forth, and we are cleansed and purified, being called to a life of love and purity.
It is necessary to say to those still in wickedness to cleanse their hands and purify their hearts, for they have become diverse and multiform in sin.

The prophet will preach to those who have escaped the shame of sin and follow a life of love, saying 'Arise, Jerusalem, for your light has come and the glory of the Lord has risen upon you.' (Isaiah 60:1)
For people have fallen into deep sin, overcome by the darkness of ignorance, and it is necessary for God to appear before us and save us.

We cry out to Him, 'Why have you withdrawn from us, Lord, and overlooked us in times of trouble?' (Psalm 44:23) for the Savior has not yet taken on our likeness, and is far from us according to the word of His incarnation.
The prophet Isaiah speaks about the existence of the Only-Begotten, and asks what generation will be able to describe it.

The Savior, born of a woman, appeared to us in our time of great affliction, to save the human being born of a woman, and having freed us from the bonds of death, teaches us to say: Where is your victory, death? Where is your sting, Hades? (1 Corinthians 15:55)

For he not only gives us the gift of resurrection, but also destroys the sting of Hades, that is, sin; he says: Behold, I have given you authority to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing will harm you. (Luke 10:19)
This is one of the achievements of our Savior's presence, and it is a great comfort to us. Therefore, all dignity on earth is governed, and the darkness of ignorance has been dispelled.
The Psalmist, foreseeing this with the power of the divine Spirit, said: Justice and abundance of peace will arise in his days, until the moon is no more.
If we, being enemies, are reconciled to God through the death of his Son, an abundance of peace will arise for us.
When this happens, it is necessary for the moon to be abolished, that is, the ruler of night and darkness, called moon here in a figurative sense.
Therefore, such great and numerous lights shine for us, and the light of our divine festival shines, and again the bright festival draws us to itself.
It is clear that we should turn away from shameful things, as the wise advisor says: 'Wash and become clean, remove wickedness from your souls.' (Isaiah 1:16)
The Proverb writer's words also come to mind, 'There is a time for everything, and a season for every matter.' (Ecclesiastes 3:1)
If this is the case, then it is reasonable to agree that this time is an enemy of all wickedness, calling only those things that honor the divine law.
The judge of the contest of the righteous is God, who gives to the pious things that the eye has not seen, and the ear has not heard, and that have not entered the human heart.

Those who strive to contend in the present life, buying the title at great financial loss, and sweating in the contest, honor the winner with other wealthy prizes, but the gratitude is small, and the enjoyment only goes as far as the things of this life.
In contrast, the lovers of piety will find honor equal to their deeds, and having experienced the immense philanthropy of the Master, they will delight in goods beyond nature.
Let us then also call the lovers of piety to the annual contest of labors, and the prophet says that we should strive for virtue.
As we prepare to celebrate our holy feast, let us sound the trumpet in Zion, sanctifying a fast and proclaiming a solemn assembly.
This is a great and piercing call, a sacred trumpet that announces the presence of our holy feast.
The word of the Church is twofold, calling the ignorant to the correct understanding of divine doctrines and advising against the foolishness of works.
The trumpets are to be made of silver, symbolizing the brilliance and purity of the word. They guide us away from error and heresy, and towards the lawgiver's will.
As the prophet says, we must sanctify the fast and proclaim the healing.
How can we become workers of such things, fulfilling the divine command and striving to do the things that sanctify those who fast?
By avoiding evil, shunning shameful things, and following the brilliant and pure word of God, we can become the kind of people who truly celebrate the feast and serve the good God.
Let a disciple of Christ come among us and teach us the true manner of fasting, and we will listen to his words.
A pure and undefiled fast before God and Father is one that involves visiting orphans and widows in their affliction, and keeping oneself unspotted from the world.
It is not difficult to discover how and in what way we can fulfill these requirements.

For I believe that it is sufficient for those who are well-minded, and also the law of nature itself, teaches us to hate what seems to be contrary to divine commands, and persuades us to hold the will of the lawgiver in us.
This is the path that we must follow, and it is one that is guided by the principles of nature and the will of God.
